- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion: if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, delay forecast correction by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment spikes; weight recent sentiment (last 5 days) more heavily than older sentiment in smoothing.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by reducing standard deviation of 30d forecast by 15–20%.
